standard.title: First Nations Australians celebrating and challenging Australian identity
standard.description: investigate ways that First Nations Australian performers and composers are celebrating and/or challenging multiple perspectives of Australian identity
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored how First Nations Australians use music to continue and revitalise culture — including diverse contemporary styles, language revitalisation, and cultural knowledge-sharing in performance (AC9AMU8E02 — Y7-8). The Y9-10 step specifically concerns Australian national identity — how First Nations Australian artists engage with, celebrate and challenge perspectives on what Australia is and means.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate ways First Nations Australian performers and composers celebrate and/or challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity, evaluating innovations and the motivations behind music that advocates for social change.

nodes.label: Contributing to contemporary Australian music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate innovations in the ways First Nations Australian composers and performers are contributing to Australian contemporary music, including inter-cultural collaborations.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one First Nations Australian artist whose work makes an innovative contribution to contemporary Australian music; describe what is innovative about their contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate innovations across a range of First Nations Australian contemporary music contributions — artists working in orchestral, chamber, pop, hip-hop, country, and electronic contexts; inter-cultural collaborations that draw on First Nations Australian and non-Indigenous traditions; evaluate what each contributes to Australian contemporary music and what makes each innovative.
wider: Investigate a specific inter-cultural collaboration between a First Nations Australian artist and a non-Indigenous artist or ensemble — describe what each tradition contributes, what is new in the collaboration, and how each artist has talked about the process
Compare how two or three First Nations Australian artists in different genres each contribute to Australian contemporary music — what does each do that no other tradition could?

response_modes.reason: The breadth of First Nations Australian contributions to contemporary Australian music is the point — students who only encounter one or two examples cannot develop a picture of the full scope of these contributions. Each new genre or collaboration context reveals a different dimension of what First Nations Australian artists bring to Australian contemporary music.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Inter-cultural collaborations are particularly rich — they make visible the creative decisions involved when two traditions meet, and give students insight into how First Nations Australian artists navigate their cultural identity in mainstream contexts.
success_criteria: Can identify at least one innovative contribution by a First Nations Australian artist to contemporary Australian music
Can describe what makes the contribution innovative and how it relates to First Nations Australian identity or perspective

nodes.label: Music that advocates, educates and challenges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate and evaluate the intentions of First Nations Australian songwriters, composers and performers who use music to share knowledge, educate, protest or advocate for change.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one piece of music by a First Nations Australian artist that advocates for a specific cause or challenges a perspective on Australian identity; identify the intended message and at least two compositional choices that carry it.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian songwriters and performers use music to share knowledge, educate, protest, advocate for change, or express opinions — including music challenging action on climate change, environmental protection, social justice and racism; evaluate the intentions and effectiveness of specific works; discuss how genre and style choices affect the reach and impact of the music.
wider: Evaluate the effectiveness of a specific advocacy work — does the music achieve its stated purpose? What compositional choices help? What might be done differently?
Compare two pieces with similar advocacy aims but different stylistic approaches — which is more effective for which audience, and why?
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluating intentionality — understanding that artistic choices in advocacy music are purposeful and can be assessed for effectiveness — is the critical analytical step here. Students who can only identify the message without analysing how the music carries it remain at a surface engagement level. The ability to connect compositional choices to advocacy purposes is the analytical skill that distinguishes Y9-10 Exploring and Responding.

response_modes.reason: Build an evaluation framework for advocacy music: 'What is the intended message? Who is the intended audience? Which musical choices serve that message for that audience? How effective are those choices, and what evidence supports that evaluation?' This connects musical analysis to purpose and audience — the two dimensions that make advocacy music analytically interesting.

success_criteria: Can identify the advocacy purpose of a First Nations Australian music work
Can analyse at least two compositional choices that carry that purpose, and evaluate their effectiveness with musical reasoning

nodes.label: Mapping First Nations Australian music geographically
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use an annotated map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where specific composers and performers are working and connect their music to their cultural and geographic context.
nodes.minimum_width: Locate at least two First Nations Australian artists on a language group map; describe how each artist's work connects to their Country/Place or language group.
nodes.typical_width: Use and annotate a map of First Nations Australian language groups to identify where composers and performers are working; research and present descriptions of specific artists' music and its cultural and geographic context; make connections between Country/Place, language group and musical practice.
wider: Compare two First Nations Australian artists from different regions and language groups — how does the specificity of their Country/Place shape their music differently?
Research a First Nations Australian artist whose work directly references their language group or Country/Place — investigate how the specific geographic and cultural context is present in the music

response_modes.reason: Geographic mapping integrates the understanding of music as culturally and geographically situated with the investigation of specific artists and their work. The map makes visible the diversity of First Nations Australian cultures that the music represents — and challenges any residual assumption that First Nations Australian music is a single tradition from a single place.

success_criteria: Can locate at least two First Nations Australian artists on a language group map
Can describe how each artist's work connects to their Country/Place or cultural context
